Growth picks up, and suddenly you’re stuck choosing between an in-house recruiter, agency fees on every placement, or outsourcing the whole function, three paths with very different cost structures and incentives.[RPO recruiting](https://www.dover.com/) hands your hiring to an outside team instead of a staffing agency chasing one-off placement fees.


**TLDR:**


-


RPO hands off part or all of your recruiting to an external provider who acts as your team.


-

-

-


RPO recruiters work as embedded team members, aligning with your hiring managers and representing your brand like in-house recruiters.


-


Some solutions offer RPO benefits with vetted fractional recruiters at an average of $4,800 per hire across all roles, plus a free ATS.


## What Is RPO (Recruitment Process Outsourcing) Recruiting?


[Recruitment process outsourcing](https://www.robertwalters.us/insights/hiring-advice/blog/what-is-recruitment-process-outsourcing.html) is a hiring model where you hand off part or all of your recruiting function to an external provider. Instead of building an in-house recruitment team or calling up an agency for a single role, you partner with an RPO provider who acts as an extension of your company.


The RPO provider takes ownership of your recruitment process from start to finish. They handle sourcing candidates, screening resumes, conducting initial interviews, managing your applicant pipeline, and sometimes even onboarding new hires. They work under your employer brand, follow your hiring criteria, and integrate with your team.


## How RPO Works and Common Service Models


PO providers work with companies in different ways based on how much help you need and which recruiting tasks you want to hand off. RPO can cover full-cycle recruiting, specific tasks like sourcing, or on-demand support during hiring sprints.


## RPO vs. Traditional Staffing Agencies: Understanding the Difference


The split comes down to how recruiters work with your company. Staffing agencies operate on[placement fees](https://www.dover.com/blog/contingency-recruiting-placement-fee-incentives) , submitting candidates from their network and typically billing 15-30% of first-year salary when someone gets hired. They juggle multiple clients at once, which pushes them toward quick closes and high volume.


RPO recruiters join your team instead. They typically focus on your roles during the engagement, learning your culture and building candidate pipelines over time. Pricing usually runs through a monthly management fee or retainer, sometimes combined with a per-hire rate set well below agency levels. This model means they attend your team meetings, use your hiring tools, and represent your company like an in-house recruiter would.


The cost difference matters most when scaling. Agencies charge per hire regardless of time spent. RPO can spread costs across a longer engagement, which may lower your average cost per hire when filling multiple positions. Pick agencies for one-off senior searches. Pick RPO when you need consistent recruiting support over months.

## Key Benefits of Recruitment Process Outsourcing for Growing Companies


RPO tackles the hiring pressures that hit growing companies hardest. You get recruiting capacity that scales when building a new team and flexes down during quieter periods, without hiring or laying off internal recruiters.


The financial difference shows up quickly. Some industry estimates put[cost reductions at roughly 25-40%](https://joingenius.com/statistics/recruitment-process-outsourcing-market/) for organizations that outsource recruitment compared with traditional recruiting methods, though results vary by provider and hiring volume. You pay for hours worked instead of placement fees or full-time salaries with benefits.


Speed counts when competing for talent against larger companies. RPO recruiters can often fill roles faster through their sourcing networks and dedicated focus, though timelines vary by role and market. They’ve spent years building talent pipelines and know where to find candidates in your space.


You also get recruiting tech you might not buy on your own. Many RPO providers include ATS software, assessment tools, and reporting, depending on the engagement model. This translates to better candidate tracking, visibility into what’s working, and a smoother experience that improves your employer brand.


## The RPO Market Growth and Adoption Trends


Grand View Research valued the[global RPO market](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/recruitment-process-outsourcing-rpo-market) at $12.8 billion in 2025 and projects it could reach $31.5 billion by 2033. That forecast implies a 12.1% compound annual growth rate from 2026 to 2033, though projections like this can change as market conditions shift.


Several forces are pushing companies toward RPO. Ongoing labor shortages make it harder to fill roles without dedicated recruiting resources. The competition for specialized skills in tech, healthcare, and other fields means you need recruiters who know these markets. Companies also want to focus internal resources on their core business instead of building recruiting infrastructure.


Tech integration plays a role too. RPO providers bring recruiting software and data analytics that smaller companies wouldn’t buy separately. Both small businesses and large enterprises are adopting RPO to compete for talent without expanding headcount.


## What Has Changed in RPO in 2026


AI is now a standard part of RPO delivery, but results vary widely. June 2026 research from[ManpowerGroup Talent Solutions research](https://www.manpowergroup.com/en/news-releases/news/90-of-companies-use-ai-in-hiring-fewer-than-5-are-seeing-it-work) , developed with Everest Group and based on a survey of 80 senior leaders in the U.S. and U.K., found that more than 90% of organizations had deployed AI in talent acquisition, while fewer than 5% described their outcomes as transformational. Respondents cited change management and adoption (58%), governance and compliance concerns (55%), and data readiness (55%) as the top barriers. When assessing providers, the useful question is whether AI sits inside a working hiring process with human recruiters accountable for outcomes, or arrives as a standalone add-on.


Flexible engagement models are also gaining ground.[Grand View Research](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/recruitment-process-outsourcing-rpo-market) expects on-demand RPO to be the fastest-growing contract type, at a projected CAGR of approximately 17.0% through 2033. For startups with uneven hiring volume, that shift favors selective or hourly support over multi-year, full-cycle contracts. Rules on automated screening are also tightening in several jurisdictions, so it is worth asking any provider how AI-assisted screening decisions are reviewed by a person.


## When Should Your Company Consider RPO?


RPO works best when you face specific recruiting challenges that your current setup can’t solve.


If you just closed a funding round and need to double headcount within 12 months, your existing team probably can’t keep up. Bringing on recruiters takes time, and you’ll lose months to hiring and training. RPO can give you recruiting capacity that scales with your growth sooner than building a team in-house.


High-volume hiring across multiple roles or geographies also calls for RPO. Filling 10+ positions at once requires dedicated sourcing and pipeline work. A small internal team gets overwhelmed. RPO providers staff up to match your volume.


Specialized roles like your first data scientist or head of sales need market knowledge your team may lack. RPO recruiters who’ve filled similar positions know where to source candidates, what comp looks like, and how to close them.


When slow time-to-fill costs you offers or delays product launches, RPO can speed things up through focused attention and proven sourcing channels.


Finally, if your hiring fluctuates by quarter, paying for[full-time recruiters](https://www.dover.com/blog/15-20-rule-startup-recruiter) year-round makes little sense. On-demand RPO lets you pay only when you’re actually hiring.


## RPO Pricing Models and Cost Structure


RPO pricing varies by provider and the scope of recruiting support you need. Monthly retainers charge a flat fee covering agreed-upon roles or hiring volume. Cost-per-hire models bill for each completed placement, similar to agencies but at lower rates. Hourly arrangements let you pay for time spent on recruiting activities, scaling costs with actual work done.


Agency fees typically run 15-30% of first-year salary, roughly $15,000-$30,000 on a $100,000 role. Some hourly fractional recruiting marketplaces average $4,800 per hire across all roles, though costs vary by role complexity, hiring volume, and service scope. Executive searches cost more than high-volume entry-level recruiting. For startups looking to control costs while accessing expert recruiting help,[hourly fractional recruiters](https://www.dover.com/blog/fractional-recruiter-cost) offer flexibility without long-term commitments.


## How to Choose the Right RPO Provider for Your Organization


Look for providers who’ve[worked with companies at your stage](https://www.dover.com/blog/how-to-choose-the-right-recruiter-for-your-startup) and in your industry. An RPO partner who’s filled technical roles at Series A startups faces different challenges than one recruiting for Fortune 500 enterprises. Ask for[case studies and references](https://www.dover.com/blog/how-to-vet-external-recruiters-for-your-startup) from similar companies.


Check their tech stack. You want a provider with an ATS that integrates with your tools, sourcing software that reaches passive candidates, and reporting dashboards that show real-time metrics. Ask to see their recruiting tools during initial calls.


Cultural fit matters more than most companies realize. Your RPO recruiters will represent your employer brand to candidates. Talk through their communication style, values around candidate experience, and how they handle feedback. Get a sense of whether they’ll mesh with your team.


Transparency separates strong providers from weak ones. Ask to see their average time-to-fill by role type, candidate-to-interview ratios, and offer acceptance rates. Good providers share performance data upfront. Watch out for vague promises without numbers backing them up.


Match the pricing model to your hiring patterns. Retainers work when you have consistent volume. Hourly rates make sense when hiring fluctuates month to month.

## FAQs


### What’s the main difference between full-cycle RPO and on-demand RPO?


Full-cycle RPO covers your entire recruiting process (job descriptions through offers) and works best for high-volume hiring, while on-demand RPO gives you recruiting help only when needed with no long-term contract, popular with startups that have variable hiring patterns.


### How does on-demand fractional recruiting differ from traditional RPO?


Traditional RPO typically runs on longer contracts with a provider embedded across your hiring process, while on-demand fractional recruiting bills by the hour with no long-term commitment. Some marketplaces pair vetted fractional recruiters with a free ATS, averaging $4,800 per hire across all roles, though costs vary by role complexity and recruiter.


### Do I need an ATS before bringing in a fractional recruiter?


Not strictly, but it often helps. An ATS gives the recruiter and your hiring team one shared view of the pipeline, so candidate status, interview feedback, and outreach history stay in one place. Without one, coordination tends to happen over email and spreadsheets, which can slow decisions and lead to duplicate outreach. Some providers, Dover among them, pair a free ATS with on-demand recruiters so both work in the same system from the first role.


## Final Thoughts on Building Your Recruiting Strategy


[RPO recruiting](https://www.dover.com/) makes the most sense when hiring starts to outpace your internal capacity or when you need expertise your team does not yet have. If you are scaling after a fundraise, building out a new function, or hiring for specialized roles, bringing in external recruiting support can help you move faster without committing to full-time headcount too early. The key is choosing a model that fits your volume, budget, and growth plans, with a shared ATS as the foundation and recruiting capacity layered on top when you need it. Dover is one example of that approach, pairing a free ATS with on-demand fractional recruiters in one shared system, with no long-term contracts.
